question.question: If instructed to place more pieces than remain, can you use proxies or choose to place fewer than available, and does shortage waive costs or Eyrie obligations?

expected.expected_answer: No proxies; pieces finite. Must place maximum possible, not choose fewer. Costs/prerequisites not waived; required Decree action still must fully complete or turmoil.

source_passages.section: Actions — Shared movement, crafting and battle; finite pieces and prompted shortages
source_passages.quotation: Removed faction pieces normally return to supply; tracked pieces return to the **rightmost empty track space**. Placement normally takes pieces from supply, or leftmost on a track. Items removed from the game are removed permanently. Pieces are finite: no proxies. When an instruction cannot place/take/remove all prompted pieces, **you must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer**; this never waives costs or prerequisites, nor the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects. (1.5, G.20, G.24.)

source_passages.section: Actions — Eyrie Dynasties (7), handling an incomplete Decree action
source_passages.quotation: If a prompted placement runs short, place the maximum possible first, as clarified in **FAQ & Rulings**. If the required action cannot be completed fully for any reason (including warrior/building supply), immediately enter **Turmoil**; do not skip that card or continue other Decree columns. With Charismatic and only one warrior available, place that one, then enter Turmoil: one does not fulfill the required two.

source_passages.section: FAQ & Rulings — Charismatic and a supply shortage
source_passages.quotation: - **Charismatic and a supply shortage:** When a legal Decree Recruit requires two warriors but only one remains in supply, place that warrior first. Then enter Turmoil because the required two were not placed. Maximum-possible placement does not fulfill an incomplete Decree action. (FAQ under 7.7 and 7.8.2; Law 1.5.4.)

answer.ruling: Pieces are finite and proxies cannot be used. If an instruction prompts placement of more pieces than remain, place the maximum possible; you cannot voluntarily place fewer than are available.

answer.ruling: A shortage does not waive the Eyrie's obligation to complete its Decree action. Place the maximum possible first, then enter Turmoil because the required action remains incomplete; do not skip the card or continue to another Decree column. If Charismatic requires two warriors and only one remains, place that one and enter Turmoil; it does not satisfy the two-warrior requirement.
